propositions: Core push delivery must enforce exactly five retry cycles plus one conditional terminal push, with strict mode raising PushDeliveryError for non-fast-forward rejections and transport failures classified by distinct stable reasons.
Strict delivery is opt-in via keyword-only strict=False default, catchable at the call site, and only the private Python module adapter translates PushDeliveryError to stderr and nonzero exit.

All pre-existing library callers, CLI commands, MCP tools, and store-write operations (event append, batch append, import, close, delete, compact, claim) must retain best-effort semantics by omitting strict or passing strict=False.
Strict failure does not write ticket events, emit BRIDGE_ALERT, or mutate HEAD/worktree; paired best-effort calls return None without side effects.
The retry-budget and strict-delivery implementation is owned by Python core and functions identically across brew, pip, and MCP-server installs without workflow-local shell logic.

Deterministic contention tests verify exactly six total push attempts (five in-loop rejections followed by one terminal push only if the fifth rejection produced a clean merge), and earlier success exits without a terminal push.
